root_cause.text: The BUG_ON() in pn_socket_autobind() incorrectly assumes that a -EINVAL return from pn_socket_bind() always means the socket was already bound with a non-zero port, but pn_socket_bind() can also return -EINVAL when sk_state is not TCP_CLOSE on an unbound socket, causing a crash when the port is zero.
root_cause.evidence: The patch description states: "However pn_socket_bind() also returns -EINVAL when sk->sk_state is not TCP_CLOSE, even when the socket has never been bound and pn_port() is still 0. In that case the BUG_ON() fires and panics the kernel from a user-triggerable path." The fix replaces the unconditional BUG_ON with a check that returns -EINVAL when the port is still zero.
